analysis:
The PR changes two lines in docs/reference/configuration.md (lines 157 and 161 on both sides), in the Add-on hold table. It is documentation only, with no code or control changes.

Line 157: the DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET row now says the variable is "Tests only, though every build reads it". This is more accurate documentation of existing behavior. Release builds honor an absolute socket path override. The doc also states the variable is not in the LaunchAgent passthrough list, so the installed daemon always uses the default socket.

This touches TB-012 (local add-on hold socket), A-018 and T-059 (a local process holding the provider out of routing). Whether a same-UID process can set the variable for a foreground or CLI-started provider and redirect the socket is existing behavior. The doc change discloses it and does not create it. I saw no source for AddonHoldPaths or AddonPeerPolicy, so I could not check that the signature or peer check still gates a redirected socket in release builds. That is an integration question for reviewers of the code, not a regression introduced here.

Line 161: the settle bound is renamed to addonHoldSettleTimeoutDefault, and the row now says a load still running after the bound is waited for, not abandoned. This describes the hold semantics and relates to T-059 availability. The matching code is not in this batch, so the doc-to-code match is unverified.

The unchanged base and head context on prefix cache, MiMo, Qwen4, GLM and App Attest worker flags was skimmed. It did not change, and I saw no security-relevant edits.

No findings. needs_deeper_review is true only because the code behind the documented add-on hold behavior (the release-build socket override and the load-settle wait) was not supplied.
